title.title: A first $L^p$ bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform
title.subtitle: Claim: $\mathrm{p.v.}\int f_1(x-t)\,f_2(x-2t)\,f_3(x-3t)\,dt/t$ is bounded $L^3 \times L^3 \times L^3 \to L^1$

plain: Multiply three signals read at evenly spaced points, then average: can the result blow up?

beats.text: Three functions read at a four-term progression with common gap $t$
Lacey and Thiele tamed two functions; a third brings quadratic structure
The claim: $L^3 \times L^3 \times L^3 \to L^1$, the first bound at any exponent

steps: A quadratic inverse theorem finds the hidden curved structure
Work locally, in charts where that curvature is under control
Sum the charts over scales without losing a factor each time
